dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The 31-May cluster consists of exactly 17 annual rows (`term_days=365`), all from DLR-104 (8) and DLR-219 (9), uploaded in a single 21:00 batch window.
Annual rows reconcile to the import log exactly — May: DLR-104 = 8 rows / $723.42, DLR-219 = 9 rows / $782.87. Across all months: 90 annual rows = 90 import-log rows, $0.00 reconciliation difference.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: No backdating: all 90 annual rows have effective-month equal to posted-month, and `posted_at` is never earlier than `effective_event_date`. May batch effective dates span May 1–28.
The sole real issue is cosmetic: posting-date trend reports will show a spike that vanishes when re-keyed to `effective_event_date`.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations:
## Rejected Hypotheses
- **Duplicate revenue:** Killed by fully unique `recharge_id`/`source_event_id`, zero content duplicates on (subscriber, date, amount, plan), and exact reconciliation across all 41 import files.

## Unknowns and Decision-Changing Evidence
- **Revenue-recognition basis:** If the trend pack uses `posted_at` as the recognition date rather than `effective_event_date`, the month-end spike is a benign visual artifact — but the GL isn't in the data to confirm.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: The cheapest improvement is to re-key the trend-pack charts on `effective_event_date` instead of `posted_at` (a reversible reporting change) and verify the 31-May spike flattens.
Separately, confirm the recognition basis with Revenue Assurance and the dealer-region mapping in the dealer master before any external commentary.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: No escalation warranted. The 31-May cluster of 17 annual renewals is a routine month-end batch-posting by two West-region dealers (DLR-104 and DLR-219), not duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect.
Do not reverse, hold, or question any of the 17 postings — they are reconciled, unique, and represent real revenue.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “I independently verified Kavya Iyer's email claims against the data — every assertion holds” is overstated because the submission itself says the contract permitting monthly submission is unavailable and dealer-region mapping is not independently confirmed.

“The revenue is genuine” is stronger than the tested evidence supports: uniqueness, reconciliation, timing, and pricing support absence of detected duplication or posting irregularity, but do not establish the underlying commercial validity of every renewal.

“Date-stuffing or manipulated reporting: Killed” and “Pipeline defect: Killed” are too categorical. The tests substantially reduce those hypotheses for the tested fields and files, but cannot eliminate all forms of reporting manipulation or pipeline defects.

The recommendation to “not ... question any of the 17 postings” is somewhat absolute while GL recognition basis, contract terms, and dealer master mapping remain unresolved. No direct downstream trend-pack test is shown; flattening is proposed for later verification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate revenue, reporting manipulation, and pipeline defect, and tested them with identifiers, reconciliation, timing, and accepted-row checks. The main missed or insufficiently bounded alternative is that the postings may be valid operationally but still require accounting or contractual review; the available data cannot prove underlying revenue validity or recognition treatment.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the categorical conclusions about “genuine” revenue and hypotheses being “killed” with bounded claims, then directly validate the GL recognition basis and contract/dealer-master mappings while producing the effective_event_date versus posted_at trend comparison.

"Pre-auth terminations tripled: 24.0% under NOVA-S1 vs 7.9% South-LEGACY and 6.9% other regions; auth error codes (TOKEN_MISMATCH, ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT, PIN_RETRY_LIMIT) hit 13.1% of NOVA sessions" | `ivr_interactions.jsonl`

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop is predominantly a measurement and authentication artifact — pre-authentication failures tripled under NOVA-S1, and those failed sessions never generate CareDesk cases"
"CAUSAL CLAIMS (tentative): Auth/prompt defects plus the case-exclusion rule cause much of the drop; new self-service capabilities cause a genuine but smaller portion."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Some genuine self-service deflection exists (new `balance_check` and `pack_info` stages), so the honest read is mixed — not 'all fake,' but certainly not the clean win the email presents."
"UNKNOWNS: 7-day repeat-contact rate; exact containment metric denominator definition; operational fate of a pre-auth failure."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally. Keep the South pilot running (reversible) so we can gather corrected data"
"reconcile IVR sessions to CareDesk cases so nothing is invisible, and re-evaluate over two full weeks against an E/N/W control before any rollout decision."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What are the exact numerator and denominator of the case-containment dashboard, and does the denominator include sessions that terminate before subscriber authentication?"
"Under NOVA-S1, what conditions must be met for a session to create a CareDesk case vs. resolve-and-close vs. transfer to an agent"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Tripled pre-auth failures are would-be complaints" is not established: authentication abandonment may represent a complaint, a routine service request, an accidental exit, or a successfully resolved need through another channel.

"The drop is predominantly a measurement and authentication artifact" is plausible and well supported by the case-creation gap, but predominance is not demonstrated without linked journey outcomes, repeat contacts, or sampled call review.

"Meanwhile, network outages stayed flat, meaning the underlying problems did not improve" overstates the service-event evidence: unchanged outage exposure supports no observed improvement in that measured problem, but does not establish that all underlying customer problems were unchanged.

"Auth/prompt defects plus the case-exclusion rule cause much of the drop" remains a causal inference rather than a demonstrated effect because the submission does not show matched subscriber-level journeys or a counterfactual.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—that new NOVA self-service stages produced some genuine deflection—by explicitly noting `balance_check` and `pack_info` and describing the result as mixed. It nevertheless missed a fuller alternative in which some pre-authentication abandonment is benign or reflects logging/session-volume changes rather than lost complaints; the proposed repeat-contact and journey-linkage checks would help distinguish these possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Directly link IVR sessions to downstream outcomes and review a sample of pre-authentication failures, separating complaint journeys from routine requests, successful later contacts, accidental exits, and unresolved friction before describing the suppression as predominantly lost complaints.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `inverter_events.csv` and specific fields: `impact_mw = 0`, `cleared = yes`, severity, duration, inverter IDs, and event count.
It distinguishes uncertainty by stating that completeness and whether `impact_mw` is populated cannot be confirmed from the export alone.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests the main failure hypothesis against zero impact, cleared status, short duration, low severity, distinct inverters, and lack of recurrence.
It considers two plausible innocent explanations: an incomplete export and a zero-valued impact field that may not be populated.
The reasoning is primarily based on one event-export channel rather than an actual independent-channel cross-check.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly limits its conclusion to what the file shows: 'Nothing in this file shows impact, recurrence, or an open fault.'
It proposes the smallest decision-changing checks: confirm the export is complete and confirm that `impact_mw` is actively computed.
It avoids claiming that the event names prove equipment failure and appropriately treats wording as weak evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation 'Do not escalate' follows from zero impact, self-clearing, low severity, short duration, and no recurrence.
The proposed 'cheap, five-minute check' is proportionate and discriminating, with an explicit stopping rule: 'If it is, stop here.'

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the strongest supported interpretation: no demonstrated plant problem, no escalation, and only a low-priority completeness check.
It does not invent a mechanism from the seven-minute communications warning or the mixed event names.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that four events over nine days is 'thin' for a multi-inverter plant is a contextual judgment without a supplied expected event baseline, though it is not used to drive escalation.

The statement that wording 'is not evidence of a fault' is slightly too absolute; wording is weak evidence by itself, but the submission's broader point that it does not establish a fault is well supported.
The claim of 'zero recurrence' is valid for the displayed export, but should remain scoped to that file and window; the submission largely makes that scope clear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, or `impact_mw` may be defaulted to zero; under that interpretation the apparent benignity cannot yet be trusted. The analyst identifies both possibilities and proposes inexpensive checks before stopping.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the exact source-system validation needed for `impact_mw`—for example, compare one event with the corresponding plant telemetry or confirm the field's calculation/population rule—while keeping the completeness check as the first action.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Penalty Rs 662,444 (28 May) → Rs 453,086 (29 May) = −31.6%" is tied to dispatch_blocks.csv and AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md.
The same-day calculation is explicitly tied to base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual generation, and the 12 pilot_revision blocks in dispatch_blocks.csv.
The submission identifies the 28/29 May weather and firmware fields and distinguishes the 4 June firmware confounder.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: "The 31.6% is a cross-day comparison" correctly identifies the central comparison problem.
It constructs a same-day base-versus-submitted counterfactual and localizes the difference to the 12 revised blocks.

It considers hindsight tuning, firmware changes, energy-value tradeoffs, and the possibility that the result is a one-day fluke, though some alternative explanations are identified more than fully tested.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "it rests on a sample of exactly one pilot day" appropriately limits generalization.
The submission distinguishes the identifiable within-day mechanical effect from unknown repeatability, ex-ante forecast skill, and net commercial value.
It avoids claiming that the 31.6% is a controlled causal estimate and recommends replication before expansion.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Keep the pilot running" preserves the potentially useful intervention rather than overcorrecting to no value.
The proposed next test extends the same-day counterfactual across multiple high-wind stow days, controls firmware, preregisters qualifying days, and reports the distribution of effects.
The recommendation to switch from penalty-only to net commercial value is directly responsive to the identified energy-value limitation.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion reports the smaller same-day benefit, "~17.5% on one weather-matched day," rather than accepting the 31.6% headline.
It accurately separates "pilot day performed better" from proof that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction.
It retains a positive but appropriately limited conclusion: continue the pilot, but do not scale or publish the headline without replication.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the within-day effect is fully "identifiable" is somewhat stronger than warranted: it is a well-defined fixed-actual-generation schedule comparison, but its causal interpretation still depends on the base schedule being a valid no-pilot counterfactual and does not establish ex-ante forecast skill.
Calling the 28/29 May comparison "clean" or "weather-matched" should be qualified because the weather values are close rather than identical and residual operational differences may remain.
The stated reduction is arithmetically imprecise: Rs 549,664 − Rs 453,086 equals Rs 96,578, not Rs 96,476, although the approximate 17.5% percentage is essentially unaffected.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot likely did reduce the modeled 29 May penalty under the fixed-actual-generation, base-versus-submitted comparison, but the result could partly reflect a one-off or hindsight-informed schedule revision and may not recur on other days; moreover, lower penalty does not necessarily mean higher net commercial value because energy value may have been forgone.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the timestamped ex-ante submission process and replicate the base-versus-submitted calculation across several pre-registered high-wind days while holding firmware and other operational conditions constant, including net energy value in the outcome.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies specific sources in its evidence table, including “country_tariff_matrix.xlsx (Swiss Matrix),” “product_master_current.xlsx (Read Me),” and “canonical-schema-v0.3.md.”
It also identifies limitations: “The effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001” is missing and “the matrix has no duty column.”

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly tests competing explanations, including “`90211000` is a keying error for `90211090`,” “Helios is the source of truth,” and “A string mismatch inherently proves a compliance failure.”
It gives a coherent alternative mechanism: “At the harmonised six-digit level both are `902110`; the mismatch exists only in the national tail digits, which are jurisdiction-specific by design.”

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The response appropriately acknowledges uncertainty by listing “Code-system identifier and nomenclature version stamped on each code” and the “effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling” as missing evidence.

However, it states categorically that the code is “exactly the Swiss-approved tariff code” and that the issue “is not a broker error,” despite acknowledging that authoritative Tares or ruling confirmation is still absent.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains that Helios contains a “commercial commodity code,” is “migration-mapped,” and is “not customs-ruling status.”
It identifies the comparator’s structural limitation: “Schema models no code-system / nomenclature version / effective date — the comparator is structurally blind.”
The proposed mechanism correctly distinguishes Swiss national digits from the shared HS6 value `902110`.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed remediation is proportionate and reversible: “Fix the comparator to compare within one nomenclature (or normalise to HS6 before flagging) and make it code-system- and effective-date-aware.”
The action is somewhat overconfident because it says “Do not raise it to the broker as an error” and “close the flag” before the missing Tares or binding-ruling evidence is obtained.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The declared code `90211000` is exactly the Swiss-approved tariff code for P1001, current on the 2025-11-04 entry date” is supported only by the internal Swiss Matrix, while the submission itself says authoritative Tares or ruling confirmation is missing.

“This is a cross-code-system false positive, not a broker error” is well supported as the leading explanation but is stated more definitively than the available authoritative classification evidence permits.
“Do not escalate as a declaration error” and “close the flag” should be conditional on confirming the authoritative Swiss classification and ensuring no separate product-classification issue exists.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss Matrix or product-to-code mapping could itself be stale or incorrect, or `90211000` could be an incorrect declaration despite the apparent jurisdictional mismatch. This alternative is less supported than the benign cross-nomenclature explanation but cannot be fully rejected without the effective-dated Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the conclusion and closure action explicitly conditional: obtain and cite the authoritative effective-dated Swiss Tares or binding-ruling record, then document the code-system and version mapping before closing the flag.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "preference is ... questionable on its face" because the line is declared US origin is somewhat overstated: manufacturing country is not preferential origin, which the submission otherwise correctly explains.

The statement that the line should be "treated as non-preferential (MFN) for now" is operationally reasonable as a hold position, but should explicitly distinguish provisional non-granting from a finding that the good is definitively non-originating.

Therefore, the preference claim could ultimately be valid even though it is not established by the current packet or register linkage.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Specify the exact preference programme and origin criterion, then trace the shipment's actual supplier and obtain the corresponding current declaration before making the provisional non-preferential treatment final.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"'The data is broken — throw it out' ... arithmetic is clean ... The problem is timestamp semantics, not data integrity"
"'COA MISSING proves batches were released without certificates' ... needs a live-portal spot-check before alleging anything"

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The data catalog definition of `qcore_release_ts` ... This is the decisive check"
"A live-QCore spot-check of 5–10 `02:10:00` batches"
"A fresher, source-aligned extract (or event-level QCore log)"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "QCore records the release date and defaults the time to its batch boundary" is stronger than the cited snapshot-time evidence unless the catalog or event-log comparison directly establishes that semantic.
"The real process is fast" is not yet established: it relies on only 23 routine rows after excluding most rows whose timestamp semantics remain unverified, creating possible selection bias.
"HOLD is a receipt-date artifact" is an inference from the date separation; the evidence establishes censoring and temporal imbalance, not necessarily that the HOLD population is merely an artifact.
The COA/MISSING interpretation as "likely CertVault nightly-index lag" is appropriately marked medium confidence but remains speculative until the proposed live-portal check is performed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could reflect a genuine scheduled release process, coarse time rounding, or an interface commit rather than a defaulted decision time. The elevated cycle time could therefore combine real workflow delay with extract/interface timing; only event-level decision and evidence-available timestamps can discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Downgrade the 5.5-hour result from "the real process" to a provisional sensitivity result, then obtain a batch-level event log or live-QCore comparison containing the true disposition/decision timestamp, evidence-available timestamp, and source snapshot time for a small stratified sample including 02:10 and non-02:10 records.

citations: "Confirmed manufacturer part numbers on the 11 blank requests"
"Live local-CMMS availability for HA-0022 and ME-0006"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission calls eight items "transfer-ready now" and recommends raising transfers and cancelling external POs today even though it also reports that the global stock view is approximately four weeks stale; no current local-CMMS confirmation is provided for the supposedly actionable stock.
There is an internal count inconsistency: the candidate table says "8 requests with blank part number," while the evidence table says "11/24 requests have blank manufacturer_part_no."

The statement that confirmed part numbers would "flip most straight to actionable" is not established; a part number alone does not resolve revision, qualification, reservation, or current availability constraints.

The $20,536 figure is presented as firm saving without clearly showing that the transfer quantity, current availability, reservation state, and PO cancellation status were independently confirmed for each of the eight items.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analysis may have identified eight strong semantic/catalog candidates rather than eight currently actionable transfers. Given the stale MaintStar snapshot, some or all should remain provisional until live availability and reservation checks are completed; the 11 blank-part-number requests also cannot safely be assumed to become actionable merely from later identity confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reclassify the eight items as candidates pending a single live transaction-level validation, then obtain current local-CMMS availability/reservation and open-PO cancellation status for each before authorizing any transfer or cancellation; reconcile the 8-versus-11 blank-part-number count at the same time.
